name: Achish
description: King living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David fled that day for fear of Saul and went to Achish the king of Gath, and the servants of Achish knew him by the song, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

points: David passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath, every man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife. When it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David said to Achish, If I have found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee? So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David and his men went up and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt; and David smote the land, left neither man nor woman alive, took away the sheep, the oxen, the asses, the camels, and the apparel, and returned to Achish.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever. So the session closes with David departed out of the presence of Saul, dwelling with Achish in the land of the Philistines at Gath.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: The Philistines gathered all their armies to Aphek, and Israel pitched by a fountain in Jezreel. David and his men passed on in the rearward with Achish, and the princes of the Philistines demanded, What do these Hebrews here?

Achish told David, As the Lord liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host is good in my sight; I have not found evil in thee. Nevertheless the lords favour thee not: return, and go in peace. David protested, What have I done, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king? But Achish answered that though David was good in his sight as an angel of God, the princes had said he shall not go up with us to the battle. So David and his men rose up early and returned into the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

One of the things to take from this reading is that they have more sense than we do. The lords of the Philistines told Achish, No, he cannot go to battle with us, because we will always be looking over our shoulders wondering if he is going to change his mind and go back unto his people.
